title: Low-degree weight and noise stability
statement: Let $n$ and $k$ be natural numbers, let $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, and let $0<\rho\le1$. Write $W_{\le k}(f)=\sum_{|S|\le k}\widehat f(S)^2$, where $\widehat f(S)$ is the uniform Fourier coefficient, and let $\operatorname{Stab}_\rho(f)=\mathbb E[f(X)f(Y)]$ for a uniform $X$ and a $Y$ obtained by independently retaining each coordinate of $X$ with probability $(1+\rho)/2$ and flipping it otherwise. Then $\rho^k W_{\le k}(f)\le\operatorname{Stab}_\rho(f)$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional Boolean cube
